role: MainActor @Observable singleton that makes the iPhone advertise as a standard BLE Heart Rate (0x180D) + Cycling Power (0x1818) peripheral so Zwift/other trainer apps can pair and receive the workout's live HR and power.
types: ZwiftPeripheralBroadcaster: class (@Observable @MainActor NSObject) — lazily-created CBPeripheralManager, service setup, per-tick value push
ZwiftPeripheralBroadcaster: extension — CBPeripheralManagerDelegate conformance (state, subscribe/unsubscribe, advertising result)
state: ble:service 1818 (Cycling Power) char 2A63 CP Measurement (notify), 2A65 CP Feature (read, 0x00000000), 2A5D Sensor Location (read, 0x06 hip)
static CBUUID constants heartRateService, heartRateMeasurementChar_UUID, cyclingPowerService, cyclingPowerMeasurementChar_UUID, cyclingPowerFeatureChar_UUID, sensorLocationChar_UUID
toplevel: static let shared = ZwiftPeripheralBroadcaster() lazily constructs the singleton; stored properties default isAdvertising=false, subscriberCount=0, wantsBroadcast=false, all CB objects nil; CBUUID statics are nonisolated constants. Advertised local name is the literal "Emuqu" (line 93).

flags.text: cpFeatureChar and sensorLocationChar are assigned in cyclingPowerService() but never read anywhere in the repo (grep finds only the declaration and the assignment); they are leftover state.

docs/FLOWCHART.md names ZwiftPeripheralBroadcaster.shared.start()/stop() (no such methods; they are startBroadcasting/stopBroadcasting) and says update(heartRate:powerWatts:) runs 'only when enableZwiftBroadcast', but the ticker calls update every tick unconditionally and it is a no-op only because isAdvertising is false.

units.does: NSObject init; deliberately does not create the CBPeripheralManager so the Bluetooth-peripheral permission prompt is not shown until the user's first broadcast.
units.entry: Invoked once by the static initializer of ZwiftPeripheralBroadcaster.shared (line 31) when AppDependencies.collection.zwiftPeripheralBroadcaster first returns the shared instance.

units.does: Records wantsBroadcast=true, lazily creates the peripheral manager, and if the radio is poweredOn and not already advertising: removes all previously registered services, re-adds HRS+CPS services and starts advertising local name "Emuqu" with both service UUIDs, then sets isAdvertising=true (before CoreBluetooth confirms). Called from WorkoutSessionLifecycle.deferZwiftBroadcast (only when settings.enableZwiftBroadcast) and re-entered from radioStateChanged when the radio turns on.

branches.cond: peripheral manager state is not .poweredOn (e.g. .unknown right after creation, .poweredOff, .unauthorized)
branches.effect: false: logs 'Waiting for Bluetooth' and returns; the request is carried out later by radioStateChanged only if the state becomes .poweredOn. A denied/unsupported radio never advances, so nothing is advertised and nothing tells the user. true: continue.
returns without re-adding services (idempotent); otherwise services are reset and advertising starts

flags.text: When Bluetooth permission is denied (.unauthorized) or the radio is unsupported, startBroadcasting only logs 'Waiting for Bluetooth' and radioStateChanged keeps isAdvertising=false; no user-visible error says the Zwift broadcast is not running even though enableZwiftBroadcast is on.

units.does: Returns the existing CBPeripheralManager or creates one with self as delegate on the main queue and stores it; this is the only place the manager is instantiated (and so the only place the iOS BT-peripheral permission prompt can be triggered).

branches.effect: true: returns it; false: creates, stores and returns a new one

units.does: Clears wantsBroadcast, stops advertising, removes all services, sets isAdvertising=false, empties subscribedCentrals and zeroes subscriberCount. Optional-chained so it never creates the manager. Called by WorkoutRecorder.tearDownLiveWorkoutServices at workout stop.

Per-tick push (called by WorkoutTicker.pushZwiftBroadcasterUpdate with workoutHR.currentHR and motion.powerWatts): when advertising, notifies subscribed centrals with an HR Measurement packet [flags 0x00, uint8 bpm clamped 0..255] and/or a CP Measurement packet [flags 0x0000, int16 LE watts clamped 0..2000]. The Bool result of updateValue (false when the transmit queue is full) is ignored.

branches.cond: not advertising, or no peripheral manager exists
branches.effect: returns immediately (the default path when the Zwift feature is off); otherwise continues

branches.cond: heartRate non-nil and > 0 and the HR characteristic exists
branches.effect: true: sends a 2-byte HR packet; false (nil/0 HR or services never configured): no HR notification this tick

branches.cond: powerWatts non-nil and >= 0 and the CP measurement characteristic exists
branches.effect: true: sends a 4-byte power packet (0 W is sent); false: no power notification this tick

flags.text: The HR (uint8) and Cycling Power (flags u16 + int16 LE, clamped 0..2000 W) packet encodings have no test; grep finds no reference to ZwiftPeripheralBroadcaster in EmuquTests.

units.does: Adds freshly built HRS and CPS services to the peripheral manager (no-op if the manager is nil).
Builds a primary 0x180D service with one notify-only 2A37 characteristic, stores the characteristic in hrMeasurementChar, returns the service.

Builds a primary 0x1818 service with notify 2A63 measurement, read-only 2A65 feature (4 zero bytes = no optional features) and read-only 2A5D sensor location (0x06 hip); stores the three characteristics and returns the service.
Returns a CBMutableCharacteristic with .read property, .readable permission and the given static value.
Delegate callback: captures the peripheral state and hops to the main actor to call radioStateChanged.
units.entry: CBPeripheralManagerDelegate.peripheralManagerDidUpdateState, delivered by CoreBluetooth on the main queue after the manager is created and on each radio state change.

units.does: On a radio state change: anything but .poweredOn sets isAdvertising=false; .poweredOn starts a pending broadcast if one was requested and is not running.

branches.effect: sets isAdvertising=false and returns; subscribedCentrals/subscriberCount are NOT cleared. Otherwise continues.
true: calls startBroadcasting (re-registers services and advertises); false: nothing

flags.text: When Bluetooth turns off mid-workout, radioStateChanged clears isAdvertising but leaves subscribedCentrals and subscriberCount untouched, so the 'Zwift subscriber count' AI fact keeps reporting stale subscribers until stopBroadcasting runs.

units.does: Subscribe callback: on the main actor inserts the central into subscribedCentrals and updates subscriberCount.
units.entry: CBPeripheralManagerDelegate peripheralManager(_:central:didSubscribeTo:) when a central (Zwift) enables notifications on 2A37 or 2A63.

flags.text: The subscribe callback hops to the main actor in a new Task; a didSubscribe enqueued before stopBroadcasting runs after it, re-inserting the central and leaving subscriberCount=1 after the broadcast stopped (the AI fact app.devices.zwift_broadcast.subscriber_count then reports a stale subscriber).

units.does: Unsubscribe callback: on the main actor removes the central and updates subscriberCount.
units.entry: CBPeripheralManagerDelegate peripheralManager(_:central:didUnsubscribeFrom:) when a central disables notifications.

units.does: Advertising-result callback: on error logs a warning and sets isAdvertising=false; wantsBroadcast stays true but nothing retries.

branches.effect: true: warning log + isAdvertising=false (update() then becomes a no-op for the rest of the workout unless the radio state cycles); false: nothing

flags.text: A failed startAdvertising only logs and clears isAdvertising; wantsBroadcast stays true but no retry is scheduled, so Zwift never sees the sensor for that workout and the user gets no indication.
